chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from 'Ali ibn al-Nu'man from Sa'id al-A'raj from Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him)

Regarding a man who delegates the authority of his wife to a man, he said: 'Bear witness that I have delegated the authority of so-and-so to so-and-so,' and he divorces her. Is that permissible for the man? He said: 'Yes.'

key_terms.فُلاَنَ: So-and-so (a placeholder name for the appointed agent)

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible for a husband to delegate the right of divorce to another person in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* establishes the permissibility of *tafwid al-talaq* (delegation of divorce), where a husband grants another person the authority to pronounce divorce on his behalf. Imam al-Sadiq (AS) confirms the validity of this arrangement, highlighting the flexibility in marital jurisprudence regarding the execution of divorce by a proxy. This ruling underscores the principle that the essential element is the clear intent and authorization, rather than the physical presence of the husband during the utterance.
